newsitem.title: GHANA: Malaysian consortium buys into Ghana Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian consortium buys into Ghana Telecom.

text.p: Ghana has formally privatised a 30 percent stake and the management of its telecommunications company, handing both over to G-Com Ltd, a consortium led by Telekom Malaysia Berhad, a senior official said on Tuesday.
The government has also sold a licence for a second telephone network, the official told Reuters.
There has been no official announcement on either deal.
James Adenusa, telecommunications advisor to Transport and Communications Edward Salia, said the Ghana Telecom handover took place on Thursday.
G-COM Ltd, offering $38 million, was the highest bidder at the opening of bids last December.
"A new board of directors will be appointed and will elect a new chief executive early next month," Adenusa said.

Adenusa said that on January 31, a consortium of African Communications Group, Western Wireless and Ghana National Petroleum Company, paid for and obtained an official licence to operate a second network of telephone lines.
Last December that consortium emerged as top bidder for a rival network with $10.1 million.
The idea behind a second nationwide telephone company is to create competition.
Western Wireless is a cellular provider in the United States. Based in the U.S. city of Cambridge, African Communications Group has been operating wireless card pay telephones in Tanzania since 1993.
The consortium wants to invest between $40 million and $70 million in the next five years. It pledged to install 50,000 lines in three years.
A Malaysian spokesman said in December that G-Com had pledged a major investment programme of at least 200,000 lines over the next five years.
